descriptions.text: Welcome to the $13.7 million M2 Exchange house of horrors, where despite claiming they've caught their ghost, restless spirits still perform their midnight waltz. A carnival of contradictions awaits…
According to on-chain detective ZachXBT on his personal channel, cryptocurrency exchange M2 was hacked, resulting in the theft of approximately $13 million from several on-chain hot wallets.

M2 Exchange lost $13.7 million on October 31, 2024, when an attacker gained unauthorized access to hot wallets across Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana. The breach was detected and contained within 16 minutes, with customer funds restored from corporate reserves. An access control vulnerability in M2 Exchange's hot wallet infrastructure allowed the attacker to bypass authorization and drain funds across multiple chains. The precise mechanism is not publicly disclosed, but available evidence points to centralized wallet signing authority compromise.
